key_insight: Longer on-policy distillation trajectories show diminishing supervision returns; randomizing rollout horizons reduces redundant work while retaining access to deeper response states.
engineering_relevance: Stochastic Horizons On-Policy Distillation (SH-OPD) lowers per-update compute cost while preserving batch-parallel generation and competitive reasoning performance.
method: Analyze supervision utility, cross-position transfer, and gradient structure across response depths.
Sample one shared rollout horizon per training batch instead of supervising uniformly long trajectories.
Characterize horizon-induced reweighting bias and derive a compute–reweighting trade-off.
evidence_signal: Experiments report slightly higher mathematical reasoning accuracy at approximately 45% of standard OPD’s per-update cost and competitive code generation performance at around 60% of baseline cost.
watch_item: Random horizons reweight supervision across response depths; lower per-update cost does not by itself establish lower total training cost.
paper_title: Rethinking Supervision Scaling in On-Policy Distillation: From Dense Supervision to Stochastic Horizons
